title: Issue Tracker and Agile Board
summary: Track project work items with custom workflows, fast backlog reordering, filtered search, and live boards.
statement:
Design a multi-tenant issue tracking and agile board platform used by software and operations teams to plan sprints, manage backlogs, and track work.

Functional requirements:
- Users create and update issues with custom fields, comments, and attachments, and move issues across project-specific workflow states (`Open -> In Progress -> In Review -> Done`) governed by transition rules.
- Teammates drag and drop cards to reorder backlogs containing tens of thousands of issues and see card moves and status updates on shared sprint boards in near real time.
- Support rich structured queries filtering and sorting issues across projects by status, assignee, sprint, priority, labels, and text.
- Maintain an immutable per-issue activity history of every field and status transition.

Scale to assume:
- 300,000 tenant organizations, 5 billion total issues, and 2 million concurrent active users during business hours.
- 250,000 board and filter reads per second and 35,000 issue mutations (edits, transitions, and drag-and-drop reorders) per second.
- Large monorepo projects can hold 100,000+ backlog issues and 500 engineers viewing the same active board.
hints: If a backlog stores integer positions `1..100,000`, dragging card `90,000` to position `2` rewrites `89,998` rows. What representation lets a drag-and-drop reorder update a single row, and what happens when repeated drops at the same spot run out of space?

Transactional databases excel at ACID workflow transitions, whereas inverted search indexes excel at arbitrary multi-field filter queries. If a user drags a card on a board and refreshes 100 ms later, how do you avoid showing stale state from an eventually consistent search index?
Enterprise tenants invent hundreds of custom fields per project—how do you store and index tenant-defined fields without running `ALTER TABLE` across a 5-billion-row database?
expectations: Clarifies consistency guarantees (strong ACID transitions and read-your-own-writes on boards versus sub-second eventual consistency for cross-project search), custom-field limits, and board fan-out scale.

Partitions the transactional source of truth by `tenant_id` (with dedicated shards/cells for giant enterprise tenants), enforcing workflow state-machine validators, optimistic concurrency (`version`/`ETag`), and append-only changelog + outbox writes in one transaction.

Orders cards with lexicographic fractional indexing (`LexoRank`-style variable-length strings midpoint-computed between neighbors) so single-card drags are `O(1)` writes, paired with background rank rebalancing across alternating rank buckets when string length grows.

Models tenant-defined custom fields without schema migrations using typed `JSONB`/sparse attribute columns in the primary store and bounded typed slot mappings (`string_slot_1..N`, `num_slot_1..N`) in the search index to prevent mapping explosion.

Feeds a tenant-routed search index asynchronously via `CDC`/outbox consumers for multi-attribute filter queries, while serving active sprint boards directly from the primary/read-your-writes cache or merging client-known mutation versions so dragged cards never snap backward.

Pushes compact, sequence-numbered board delta events (`issue.transitioned`, `issue.ranked`) over WebSockets/`SSE` scoped to `board_id` so 500 teammates see live moves without polling full board payloads.
Protects hot project boards from stampedes with cached board projections, cursor pagination on large backlogs, and per-tenant rate and query-cost limits.
